# Real references, real arrays and real sampling (SIM-005)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes. The six feature fixtures also run on legacy,
compact/portable and compact/GMP backends
and, except the numeric-extremes fixture, after the frontend snapshot and owned
Db are destroyed; the extremes fixture also runs at model `-O0` and `-O3`.
Expected outputs are derived by hand from the cited clauses, not captured from
llg.

Reals keep numeric semantics throughout: a real `ref` formal is the actual's
`double` cell, real arrays are `double` cells inside and across subroutines,
and comparisons use real `==`, never a bit pattern, except case equality of
real arrays (decision R05-D4). Shortreal storage rounds
to the nearest IEEE single.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `real_refs` | IEEE 1800-2009 §§13.5.2, 6.12. `add(r,0.5)` gives 1.25+0.5=1.75. Shortreal 0.1 is 0.100000001490116; times 3.0 is 0.30000000447, nearest single `3e99999a`. Forwarding through `forward` adds 1.0 then 0.25 to each element: 2.25 3.25 4.25. `look(a[2])` = 2*4.25+1 = 9.50 through two `const ref` levels. `m[1][2]` = 12 + 0.5 (run-time row index). Index 7 is out of range, so the write goes nowhere and `a` is unchanged. Record members: 0.5+1.0 = 1.50, `k` stays 3, shortreal 1.0*3 = 3.0 = `40400000`. `swap(lo,hi)` gives 2.0 1.0; `swap(lo,lo)` writes `lo` twice and leaves 2.0. Recursion: each activation adds k*0.5 for k=4..0, total 5.00. At time 2 two timed activations run in a fork: `r` = 1.75+3*0.5 = 3.25 and `a[1]` = 0-3*1.5 = -4.50; `@(a[1])` sees the time-1 write plus three reference writes: 4. |
| `real_element_copyout` | §§13.3, 13.5.1, 7.4.6. Output/inout actuals selecting a real element copy back into that cell; the selectors of the copy-out target are evaluated when the value is copied out, after the callee returns (decision S13-D1). `bump` runs for k%4 = 0,1,2,3,0, so `a[1]` is 0.50 0.25 0.25 0.25. `put` rounds 1/3 to single `3eaaaaab`. `twice` doubles 0.25 and copies 0.50 back. `move` reads `a[1][2]` = 0.25 at the call and clears `i`, so its copy-out targets `a[0][2]`: `a[1][2]` stays 0.25 and `a[0][2]` becomes 10.25 (changed: the selectors were frozen at the call, giving 10.25 0.00). With index 5 out of range the inout reads 0.0 and both copy-outs go nowhere. The time-1 copy-out 0.25+1.5 = 1.75 wakes the `a[1][3]` waiter once. Whether the time-0 copy-out of `bump(a[1][3])` also wakes it depends on which initial procedure starts first, a race 4.7 leaves open (`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L3465-3466: "active events can be taken off the Active or Reactive event region and processed in any order"); llg runs the first initial procedure to its delay first, so the waiter is not yet armed. |
| `real_array_calls` | §§7.6, 13.3-13.5, 11.4.11, 7.4.6. `scale` doubles 1.5 2.5 3.5 into 3 5 7. `total` sums 7.50 and 1+2+4 = 7.00 and its write to its input copy leaves `a[0]` = 1.50. `inout` doubles to 6 10 14; `ref` negates the middle: -10. Equality is element-wise numeric: 1 1 0. Known predicates select whole arms; the X predicate keeps equal elements 1.5 and 3.5 and yields 0.0 for 2.5 vs 9.0. `transpose` of {{1,2},{3,4}} is {{1,3},{2,4}}; row `m[1]` sums 7.00; a nested call result feeds an input formal and `transpose(transpose(n))` equals `n` (1, `m[0][1]` = 3.0). Static `mean` keeps its local array: 1/1, 3/2, 9/3. Shortreal `base/3*(i+1)` rounds to `3eaaaaab` `3f2aaaab` `3f800000`. `a = scale(a, 0.5)` reads before writing: 0.750 1.250 1.750. The timed output copies 7 8 9 back at time 2. |
| `real_array_declaration_initializers` | §§10.5, 10.9.1. `SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L13275-13277: "The variable declaration assignment is a special case of procedural assignment as it assigns a value to a variable. It allows an initial value to be placed in a variable in the same statement that declares the variable"; L13645-13646: "The expressions shall match element for element, and the braces shall match the array dimensions." Each `'{...}` row fills one row of the array in declaration order, so every element printed is the literal at its position: `r2` 1 2 3 4, `r3[0][0][1]` 2, `[1][0][0]` 5, `[1][1][1]` 8; `rr[1:0][0:1]` puts the first row at index 1 (1 2) and the second at 0 (3 4). `default: 7.5` fills every cell. Non-constant items take their values at initialization: `x` = 1.5 and `P` = 2.5 in `n1`, `n2` and `sh`; `cp` copies `r2` (declared earlier): 2 3; `f(1.0)` 2, `f(x)` 3, `f(P)` 5. `'{2{'{3{0.5}}}}` replicates 0.5 into all six cells; integral items convert to real (1 2 3, 4.5); shortreal 0.1 is 0.100000001490116, 0.10000000 at eight places. Index labels: row 0 is 1.0 except `[0][1]` = 9.0, row 1 is 2 3. Package arrays: `pr[0][1]` 2, `[1][0]` 3; `ps[0][2]` 2.5, `[1][1]` 4.5. String, chandle and record cells print their initializers (`rs2[0][1]` 2.5 2, `[1][0].a` 3.5, `[1][1].b` 4). The automatic task's arrays are initialized at each entry, so the write `lr[1][1] = 0.0` of the first call is not seen by the second: `4.5 + k` gives 5.50 then 6.50. Output agrees with industry-standard behaviour. |
| `real_array_methods` | §§7.12.1, 7.12.2. Stable numeric `sort`/`rsort`/`reverse` of {1.5,-2,4.25,0.5,-2}; the three in-place changes of `a[0]` in one time step wake its waiter once. Shortreal 0.1/0.2/0.3 sort to `3dcccccd` `3e4ccccd` `3e99999a`. `reverse` moves rows whole, then reverses row 1. A NaN keeps its position and the keys on each side sort separately: {1,3,NaN,-1,2}. Over {3,1,2,1,-0.0,0.0}: `find` x>1.5 gives 3 2; `find_index` x<2.5 gives indices 1..5; `find_first` x<2 is 1.0; `find_last_index` x==1 is 3; `min` is the first minimum -0.0 (`8000000000000000`, since 0.0 < -0.0 is false); `max` 3.0; `unique` keeps 3,1,2,-0.0 (indices 0 1 2 4, -0.0 == 0.0). Stable `sort` gives -0.0 0.0 1 1 2 3; `rsort` then `reverse` gives 0.0 ... 3.0. A dynamic array sorts to -1 0.25 0.5 2 and `find` with `e.index != 1` gives 0.50 and 2.0. With NaNs, `min` skips them (-3.0) and every NaN is unique (4). `max` of an empty queue is empty. |
| `real_sampled` | §16.9.3. Procedural `$sampled` returns the Preponed values 1.25 and shortreal 0.5 (`3f000000`). On posedges at 5..55 the samples are 2.5, 2.5, 0.0, -0.0, NaN, NaN. `$past` before the first tick is the registration value 1.25. §16.6.1 (`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L21575-21576: "The following types are not allowed: — Noninteger types (shortreal, real, and realtime)") excludes real operands, but llg serves `$past`, `$stable` and `$changed` of reals by user decision (AA-D8, as industry-standard behaviour does); `$stable` compares the samples bit for bit: 2.5/1.25 0, 2.5/2.5 1, 0.0/2.5 0, -0.0/0.0 0, NaN/-0.0 0, NaN/NaN (the same NaN) 1. Confirmed on an industry-standard simulator without the shortreal line, which it cannot compile. |
| `real_numeric_extremes` | §§6.12.2, 20.5. Conversion to integral rounds half away from zero and keeps the low target bits: 1e20 mod 2^32 = 1661992960, mod 2^64 = 7766279631452241920, 301 mod 256 = 45; -0.5 -1, 0.5 1, 1.5 2, -2.5 -3. `$rtoi` truncates: -1, 2. Policy: a nonfinite real converted to an integral type yields 0 (the standard leaves it unspecified). Shortreal: 2^24+1 rounds to 16777216, 1e40 overflows to +inf `7f800000`, 1e-45 rounds to the smallest subnormal `00000001`, -0.0 is `80000000`. The largest double times 2 is +inf; the smallest subnormal halves to +0 (ties to even). -0.0 == 0.0. NaN compares unequal and unordered; a payload NaN is still NaN. |
| `real_array_case_equality` | §7.4.3 (`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L8089, L8095: "The following operations can be performed on all arrays, packed or unpacked." ... "Equality operations on the array or slice of the array"), §11.4.5 L14775 ("These four operators compare operands bit for bit."), decision R05-D4. `ra` = {1,2,3} equals `rb` and differs from `rc` = {1,2.5,3} in element 1: `===` 1 0, `!==` 1 0, `==` 1, `!=` 1. Slices `[0:1]` hold {1,2} and {1,2.5}: 0, and `[1:2]` {2,3} and {2.5,3}: `!==` 1. Rows: `m2a === m2a` 1, `m2b` differs in `[1][1]`: 0, row 0 matches: 1. Shortreal {0.5,0.25} twice: 1 0. 0.0 against -0.0: numeric `==` 1, bit patterns differ, `===` 0. The same quiet NaN: numeric `==` 0 (NaN is unordered), equal patterns, `===` 1 and `!==` 0; `ra !== rc` holds, so `condition` prints. Industry-standard behaviour agrees on every line except the slices, where it reports `[0:1]` equal and `[1:2]` not different under both `==` and `===`, against 7.4.3; llg follows the text there. |
| `real_ref`, `real_array_value`, `real_sample` | Adopted FND-002 witnesses with quiet `$finish(0)`: 1.75, `1.25 2.50`, 1.25. |

## Negatives

| Fixture | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `neg_real_bitwise`, `neg_real_concat`, `neg_real_select`, `neg_real_edge` | §§6.12.1, 11.3.1 Table 11-1, 11.4.12, 9.4.2: bitwise operators, concatenation, selects and edge descriptors need integral operands (frontend). Adopted FND-002 `neg_real_bitwise`. |
| `neg_real_case_equality` | Table 11-1 (`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L14254-14255): case equality is not an operator of a real operand (llg; the frontend accepts the syntax). An array of reals is not a real operand (`real_array_case_equality`). |
| `neg_real_rose` | §16.9.3: `$rose`/`$fell` read a least significant bit, which a real lacks. |
| `neg_automatic_nba`, `neg_ref_nba` | §§6.21, 10.4.2, 13.5.2: no NBA to automatic variables or ref formals (adopted FND-002 witnesses). |
| `neg_real_map` | §7.12.3: reduction methods need integral array elements; the adopted FND-002 `real_map` witness is frontend-illegal. |
| `real_element_refs` | §§7.10.3, 13.5.2. Real and shortreal elements of queues, dynamic and associative arrays bind `ref` and `const ref` formals of tasks and of functions in expressions: stores reach the element at once, the reference follows `push_front` and sees other stores (8.5 at 2), its own store of 9.5 lands at the moved index (`3 q`), `@(x)` wakes on a store to the element (2), and `delete` leaves the formal private (`9 hold end`, `d 0`). Agrees with industry-standard behaviour except `seen`: 9.2.2.2.1 L11184-11185 puts the longest static prefix `q` in the `always_comb` sensitivity (some simulators keep 3.25). Real members of record elements (`ar[1].r`, `ar[1].a[k]`, `rq[0].r`) and of a run-time-indexed module record (`mr.a[k]`) are derived by hand from 13.5.2 L19143-19147; some simulators reject them as unimplemented. |
